examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Shared-medium protocols coordinate contenders. Pure ALOHA's vulnerable interval is two frame times, while slotted ALOHA restricts starts and halves it. CSMA listens before transmission but propagation delay still permits collisions. CSMA/CD collision detection needs the sender still transmitting when a worst-case round-trip signal returns. Wireless collision avoidance has different assumptions, so do not transfer Ethernet collision-detection claims uncritically.

**Key relationship:** ALOHA maximum throughput: pure 1/(2e); slotted 1/e under the standard model

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify slotted or unslotted time.
2. Draw the vulnerable interval.
3. Relate collision timing to propagation and frame duration.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For collision detection, a sender must still be transmitting when the farthest collision can return: frame transmission time must cover round-trip propagation. CSMA/CD applies to shared half-duplex Ethernet, not ordinary full-duplex switched links. Random backoff governs contention and does not guarantee a deterministic completion time.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A shared 100 Mbps medium has 3 μs one-way propagation. What minimum frame length in bits permits collision detection?

**Answer: 600.** Round-trip propagation=6 μs. Required bits=100·10⁶×6·10⁻⁶=600. A shorter transmission could finish before a far-end collision is observed.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A real standard can impose a larger minimum frame or additional timing overhead. Use the ideal model explicitly specified by the problem.

Carrier sense does not guarantee another sender has already heard a distant transmission.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Pure ALOHA vulnerable period for frame time T is:

- **A.** T
- **B.** 2T
- **C.** 4T
- **D.** T/2

**Answer: B.** A frame starting up to T before or after can overlap the target frame, giving interval 2T.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Slotted ALOHA restricts transmission starts
- **B.** CSMA cannot remove all propagation-related collisions
- **C.** CSMA/CD detects collisions while transmitting under its model
- **D.** Listening first guarantees no collision

**Answer: A, B, C.** Two stations can both hear idle before either signal reaches the other, refuting D.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

A shared-medium collision model has one-way propagation 10 µs. Minimum transmission duration to detect a far collision, in µs?



**Answer: 20.** Worst-case detection needs a round trip: 2·10=20 µs. The sender must still be transmitting then.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q55 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/medium-access?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Medium access control. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. One-way propagation delay is 500/(2×10⁸)=2.5 μs. A far-end collision can require a round trip, 5 μs, to be detected by the original sender.
2. Transmission must last at least that long: Lmin/R≥2Tprop.
3. At 10⁸ bits/s, Lmin=10⁸×5×10⁻⁶=**500 bits**.
